description: Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) + Compose Multiplatform starter — one Kotlin codebase targeting Android, iOS, and desktop with shared UI in Compose. Uses the expect/actual pattern for platform-specific APIs and Gradle Kotlin DSL for the build. For teams that want Jetpack Compose on iOS, not Dart (Flutter) or Swift.

defaults.headline: Starter Foundry KMP App
defaults.subheadline: A Kotlin Multiplatform shell with Compose UI shared across Android and iOS, plus expect/actual platform seams.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick kotlin-multiplatform when the user names KMP, Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, `expect`/`actual`, or wants Jetpack Compose on iOS. For Google's Dart-based equivalent use flutter-app. For JS-driven mobile use expo-react-native-ts. For iOS-only SwiftUI use swiftui-expo.
firstSteps: Install JDK 17+, Android Studio (Giraffe+), and Xcode 15+ on a Mac (iOS target needs macOS)
Run `./gradlew :shared:build` to confirm the shared module compiles across all targets
Add Android app module under androidApp/ and iOS app under iosApp/ — the `shared` library is consumed from both
For iOS: `./gradlew :shared:podPublishXCFramework` (or use the Kotlin Cocoapods plugin)
Add new platform APIs via the expect/actual pattern — define `expect` in commonMain, provide `actual` in androidMain + iosMain
gotchas: iOS targets require building on macOS with Xcode; Linux/Windows machines can only build Android + desktop targets.
Compose Multiplatform 1.7+ ships @Composable for iOS but a few Material APIs are still desktop/Android-only — check expect/actual coverage.
Gradle daemon + Kotlin/Native compilation are memory-hungry — bump org.gradle.jvmargs to at least -Xmx4g in gradle.properties.
Kotlin/Native freezes objects across threads in legacy memory model; this template targets the new memory model (default in Kotlin 1.9+) — DO NOT re-enable kotlin.native.binary.memoryModel=strict.
`expect` declarations must be matched by an `actual` in EVERY target source set — missing an actual in iosMain fails the iOS build only.
architectureNotes: shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/App.kt hosts the shared @Composable App() surface — this is what both androidApp and iosApp render.
Platform APIs (clipboard, secure storage, biometrics) go behind `expect fun platform(): Platform` in commonMain with `actual` implementations in androidMain + iosMain.
auth/payments/sdk slots drop JSON config at the repo root. A bootstrap function in commonMain reads those and dispatches to the right platform service via expect/actual.
Gradle KTS is the build contract — don't mix Groovy `.gradle` and Kotlin `.gradle.kts` files; it breaks IDE navigation and composite builds.
